News.title: Huge blaze erupts at oil refinery with smoke & fire seen from miles as residents told stay away & keep windows shut
News.content:
UP IN FLAMES

UP IN FLAMES Huge blaze erupts at oil refinery with smoke & fire seen from miles as residents told stay away & keep windows shut

A MASSIVE fire has broken out at a major oil refinery as locals are warned to stay indoors.

A huge blaze and billowing black smoke can be seen for miles as firefighters try to control the blaze.





Multiple explosions could be heard coming from the Geelong Refinery, an hour south west of Melbourne, Australia, around 11pm local time (2pm BST) on Wednesday.

At least 10 emergency vehicles are currently at the scene tackling the “significant” blaze which is not yet under control.

The Country Fire Authority issued a watch and act for a large swathe of Geelong urging locals to take shelter indoors immediately.



“There is a factory fire in Refinery Road, Corio,” the advice said.

“A wind change has caused the smoke to be blown towards the Northern Geelong area.”

Residents were also being urged to keep off the roads to allow emergency services to respond.

The site is one of only two operational oil refineries in the country.



It supplies more than 50 per cent of Victoria’s fuel and around 10 per cent of Australia‘s fuel.

It can process up to 120,00 barrels of oil a day, including “manufacturing petrol, diesel, LPG, jet fuel, avgas and Low Aromatic Fuel”.

It’s understood more than 1,100 people work at the site.

News.title: Chilling new details emerge after home invader seen in terrifying viral doorbell video makes first court appearance
News.content:
CHILLING new details have emerged about a home invader who terrorised a mum and daughter in a viral doorbell video.

Jason Thomas Nichols, 30, is accused of breaking into a California home after threatening to kill a pregnant mum and her son, 5, inside.





In the shocking footage, the man tries to kick down the front door of a Bay area home while screaming to be let inside.

Making his first appearance in court on Wednesday, Nichols wore a striped jail jumpsuit and was shackled at the waist.

He reportedly smiled and rolled his eyes through some of the proceedings while also thanking reporters for taking his photo.

Nichols was charged with four felonies, including burglary, assault with a deadly weapon, vandalism and making criminal threats.

A brave witness also came forward with new allegations about an encounter with Nichols and a child two days before the home invasion.

Nichols now faces a fifth charge of annoying or molesting a child under 18.

The footage of a creep breaking into the Fairfield home went viral online earlier this week.



The conversation begins innocently, as a man in a long black coat, flip flops and glasses asks the owner to “please” open the door.

The man, later identified by authorities as Jason Nichols, 30, explains: “I just want to make sure everything is OK. I just figured I would check on something.”

A woman with her child are inside the house at the time but she is too terrified to open the door.

Her husband, who isn’t at home, tries to persuade Nichols to go away via the doorcam microphone.

The owner replies: “I don’t know what you want man, get out of my house.”



That reply infuriates Nichols, who kicked the front door and started screaming in fury.

“Open this f***ing door. Where is your daughter man? Who’s in there with you. Open the door or I’m breaking it f***ing down. Is everybody in this house OK?” he rages.

The homeowner can be heard begging him to leave.



Nichols then asks in a menacing tone: “Open the door. This is my neighbourhood. Now…. Or I’ll f***ing end you. Do you understand me?”

He then aggressively rips off the doorbell while pounding the door.

During the ordeal, Nichols identifies himself as Harry Dresden from the popular Jim Butcher Dresden File novels about a private investigator/wizard.

Nichols then reportedly found a way inside the home by slipping through a sliding glass door.

Another security camera inside the house caught Nichols striding through the house, opening cupboards and doors looking for the wife and child.



The homeowner raced back to his home armed with a shovel to protect his wife and child.

He and Nichols reportedly exchanged blows causing each other head injuries, police said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fairfield police arrived just minutes later and found Nichols outside.

He was taken to a nearby hospital before being booked into jail on multiple felony charges tied to the brazen break-in attempt.

News.title: Iran using ceasefire to DIG OUT buried missile launchers, satellite pics show – as regime threatens to shut the Red Sea
News.content:
IRAN is using the temporary ceasefire to dig out missile launchers that were buried by US-Israeli blitzes of the rogue nation earlier in the war.

Shocking satellite photos reveal the ruthless regime will not rest during the pause in bombing and is instead using the truce to clear the way to its underground missile bases.





It comes as Iran threatens to unleash its Houthi proxy to block a second critical chokepoint for global trade – the Bab al-Mandab Strait, also known as the Gate of Tears.

The Gate of Tears is a crucial global shipping artery leading to the Suez Canal – around 10 per cent of all global trade passes through the strait at the mouth of the Red Sea.

The bases were strategically targeted by US and Israeli blitzes that blocked their entrances and exits.

It was part of a plan to trap Iran‘s missile launchers underground.

By blocking the ways in and out of the bases, targeted strikes intended to stop launchers from firing or re-loading.

But now the rogue nation is using the time allotted for peace talks to clear debris from the bases.

Satellite pictures show rubble being scooped up and loaded onto trucks to unblock entrances at bases in Tabriz and Khomeyn.



And US intelligence estimates suggest that around half of Tehran’s missile launchers are still intact.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said this week that operation Epic Fury had “functionally destroyed” Iran’s missile program, leaving the rogue nation “combat ineffective for years to come.”

But US officials told the Wall Street Journal that Iran may well be able to dig out and repair many of its buried missile launchers.

It comes as the US is piling more troops into the region after imposing a blockade on ships visiting Iranian ports in the Gulf.

The US is enforcing a blockade on Iranian-linked ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.



Although some ships seemed to have slipped through in the first 24 hours, the Americans insisted the vessels then complied with orders to stop or turn around.

The US blockade is a response to the Iranians refusing to reopen the Strait – free passage through the waterway was a key condition for the two-week ceasefire.

Trump has declared that the Iran war is “close to over” – hinting at talks in the next two days.

He was picked up on constantly referring to the war in the past tense in a Tuesday evening interview with Fox News.



When asked if he believed the war was really over, Trump replied: “I think it’s close to over. I view it as very close to over.”

The president doubled down by telling Sky News that a deal with Iran is “very possible” ahead of King Charles‘ state visit to the US later this month.

Israel expects the two-week ceasefire agreed last Tuesday to be extended.



But Trump reportedly told ABC News that he thought a deal would be agreed without an extension, saying: “I think you’re going to be watching an amazing two days ahead.”

Iran refused to relinquish its nuclear ambitions at last week’s crunch peace talks in Pakistan, but JD Vance is now prepared to tighten the screws for round two.

Vance said his boss was determined to remove Iran’s nuclear threat by stopping all Uranium enrichment, insisting Trump wants a “grand bargain” – not a “small deal”

If they continue to block peace, Trump’s next move may be a potentially catastrophic ground offensive by the 10,000-strong US invasion force he has shipped to the region.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 6,000 soldiers aboard the USS George H W Bush aircraft carrier and its escort ships are heading to the Middle East.



More than 3,000 crack airborne troops have already been sent to join 5,000 US Marines closing in on Iran.

News.title: England’s ‘wonkiest church’ which leans more than the Tower of Pisa needs £100k repairs or it could FALL over
News.content:
ENGLAND’S “wonkiest church” that leans more than the Tower of Pisa is in dire need of £100k repairs before it topples over.

Tourist favourite St James’ Church in the village of Dry Doddington, Lincs, tilts at 5.1 degrees – compared to the 3.99 degrees of its Italian counterpart over 1,000 miles away.





Locals consider the Grade II-listed building “Britain’s answer to The Leaning Tower of Pisa” – but there are now concerns for its future as it is need of essential renovations.

Over £100k will need to be raised to save the historic tilting place of worship as the church have ruled out correcting the angle.

The 12th century church was built originally as a “Chapel of Ease” for older residents to attend church rather than walking to a neighbouring village.

The tower, dating from the 14th century, is believed to have first shifted in the late 19th century and was underpinned in 1918 to prevent it from tilting any further.

Church warden Richard Loynes said: “The church is very much part of the village and we’re proud of its uniqueness.

“I wish we had the same levels of funding as the Leaning Tower of Pisa however – but that’s not the case and we need help.

“I’m off to Italy with the wife soon and will be visiting Pisa so I perhaps need to get speaking to them to see what the secret is.

“We do get visitors often coming along to take photos outside and people call me up asking to see inside. We have weddings there.



“I couldn’t say how many people come as I can’t see the church from where I live but is a draw for many people and we’d never want to lose the crookedness of the spire.

“We believe it has the tilt because it was built on a big heap of clay, which can get either very wet or very dry and when it’s dry it shrinks.

“The church has no foundations and was just plonked on earth. It was underpinned to make sure it doesn’t move any more.

“We think that is the most likely cause but some have said it could be on a burial ground too.

“We’re not really privy as to what happened 500-700-years-ago so there’s a few theories.



“But I think the most likely is that it was down to being built on clay.

“We are confident that is fully stable though so we will be protect that unique characteristic of our church.

“Our intention is not to correct the lean – as that is what helps make the tower and church so special.”



The tower was in danger of collapse in 2015 as the stones were eroding and was becoming a health and safety hazard.

Around £100,000 worth of work was undertaken then to save the tower but since then other parts of the building have deteriorated, including the floor.

Now the tower is in danger once again as the wooden church floor has deteriorated and the stone slabs have moved, and will need to be replaced.

Richard added: “The floor is now also rather wonky after it sunk and slabs and slates have cracked and moved too.

“We still have services but warn people about the wonky floor, so we need it replacing really for the safety of parishioners.



“As with hundreds of churches we need to raise funds, but we’re as bad, if not worse than most due to having the wonky floor.

“We are turning to the public for help.

“We are hoping to raise just over £100,000 to tackle the floor, replaster some of the walls and to upgrade the electricity as we only have one plug.”

One villager Thomas Ratledge said: “We like to think of it as Britain’s answer to The Leaning Tower of Pisa and such a historic church deserves to be saved.

“If the floor and walls get any worse than we worry for its future but we are confident and hopeful it will be protected for generations to come.

“It is a building with such unique character and is a focal point for the community all year round.”

News.title: Americans warned after urgent travel warning issued to popular European country with pristine Mediterranean views
News.content:
AMERICANS have been warned to remain vigilant while visiting a European country famous for its jaw-dropping Mediterranean views.

They need to exercise extreme caution due to the long arm of Iran’s Supreme Leader.





The US Embassy in Albania has warned American citizens of threats connected to the Tehran regime.

Iran-linked groups could target Americans and US-affiliated entities in Albania, the Tirana-based embassy’s alert said.

This includes while visiting tourist hotspots, restaurants and even shopping.

“Groups associated with Iran may seek to target entities associated with the US or Iranian opposition elements in Albania,” it explained.

“They may also target common venues, such as tourist sites, shopping malls, hotels, clubs, and restaurants.

“We encourage American citizens to exercise increased vigilance.”

Travelers concerned about their security in Albania were advised to monitor local media for updates, and to be aware of their surroundings.

American citizens should double-check their personal security plans and keep cell phones charged in case of emergency, it was also recommended.



Bajram Begaj, Albania’s president, said in early April that he was in daily contact with the National Security Council, which has been monitoring the potential threat.

He was being “informed about every situation and scenario, as well as all measures taken under security protocols,” the presidency added in a statement.

“The President of the Republic continues to communicate with the institutions responsible for public and national security, which are in constant coordination and collaboration with our partners.”

The embassy’s warning comes as experts continue to warn of Iran’s increased use of hybrid threats.

These include cyberattacks, and sabotage, reported the Center for Strategic and International Studies on April 9.



Donald Trump has indicated that peace negotiations with Iran’s leaders could resume this week.

He has also told Fox Business the war was “very close to being over”.

News.title: Tourist on honeymoon fighting for life after being attacked by shark with his leg ‘stripped of flesh’
News.content:
BEAST STRIKES Tourist on honeymoon fighting for life after being attacked by shark with his leg ‘stripped of flesh’

A MAN is fighting for his life after losing his leg to a shark attack on his honeymoon at a Brit holiday hotspot.

The Spanish newlywed suffered extreme blood loss when his leg was “stripped of flesh” after he was attacked by the vicious beast while swimming in the Maldives.



He had to have his leg amputated after being airlifted to hospital.



A family member of his wife told El Periodico Mediterraneo: “With one bite, it took all the flesh from the knee down off her husband’s leg.”

Another close friend said: “They are trying to save him, he’s in intensive care, but the medical conditions there are very precarious.”

Local news reports say the man hailed from Alicante and just gotten married.

The pair headed to the Indian Ocean paradise for their first holiday together as man and wife.

The horror incident is understood to have happened on Monday afternoon off Kooddoo, one of the inhabitated islands of Gaafu Alif Atoll.

The victim was reportedly part of a group that entered the water at a popular site near the Kooddoo fish processing plant, a location known for high shark activity.

It’s understood the man was rushed to the Ga. Atoll Hospital before being airlifted to Male, the densely-populated capital of the Maldives.

He was then admitted to an intensive care unit at ADK Hospital.



The island is popular among honeymooners but is also famous for large schools of Spinner sharks.

The involvement of a Bull shark has also not been ruled out.

Local reports claim the Kooddoo facility had not dumped fish waste for around a week which sharks often feed on.

“The sharks were likely in a heightened state of hunger and anticipation,” a source told local media.

“When the group jumped in, the entry itself may have triggered a predatory response.”



According to the wife’s family, she has filed a case of serious negligence against the tour company which they booked their experience through.

News.title: Terminally ill OAP, 81, jailed for tying up 95-year-old woman in attempted robbery to help pay for his own funeral
News.content:
RAID PLOT Terminally ill OAP, 81, jailed for tying up 95-year-old woman in attempted robbery to help pay for his own funeral

A TERMINALLY ill pensioner has been jailed after he tied up a 95-year-old woman and demanded cash to pay for his own funeral.

Edwin Morrison, 81, targeted Mary Morgan because she used to tip him the “princely sum” of £2 when he dropped off medication in his former job as a pharmacy courier.



He had been diagnosed with incurable kidney cancer in summer 2024 and told he would probably have less than two years to live.



Keen not to have his family pay for his funeral, Morrison hatched the robbery plot.

He tied Mary up in her home in Salford, Greater Manchester, with cable ties and shouted “give me your money“.

The pensioner pleaded with him to let her go and said she could not breathe as Morrison strangled her but he just told her to “shut up”.

Morrison then fled the property empty-handed after Mary’s mobile hairdresser arrived.

He has now been jailed for seven years after he pleaded guilty to attempted robbery.

Judge Peter Horgan said it was “very likely” Morrison would die in custody.

He added: “Your motivation to act in this way was utterly self-centred and without thought for the impact on anybody else.”

Manchester Crown Court heard Morrison had set up an online GoFundMe appeal titled “Help to bury me” as he outlined his health problems.



He wrote: “More or less been told to go in a corner and see my time out. I have no money to cover funeral costs and other incidentals.”

But prosecutors said Morrison was regularly gambling at his local bookies in the months before the attack.

He was also said to have expressed “concerns” about funding a new kitchen at the home where he lived with his then long-term partner.

On January 27, he tricked his way into Mary’s home by claiming he wanted to discuss the new bin collection date.

Once inside, Morrison bound her hands together while demanding cash.



He also put his hand around her throat and repeatedly asked for the woman’s money and purse.

After he was interrupted by the hairdresser, Morrison held his hands up as if he was going to grab her throat too before he fled empty-handed.

Detective Inspector Paul Davies, of Greater Mancheser Police, said: “It was a terrifying ordeal for the victim and Morrison’s actions of targeting a woman in her own home were shocking.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Her resilience and strength following this vile crime have been truly inspirational and I am glad that the investigative team have been able to get her the justice she deserves.

“I also want to commend the brave actions of her hairdresser who arrived as the crime was happening. She prevented Morrison from doing anything further, got him out of the living room and called 999 straight away.”

News.title: Are the ‘Rolex Rippers’ back? How thieves who assault men to steal watches could be prowling streets again
News.content:
CRIME WATCH Are the ‘Rolex Rippers’ back? How thieves who assault men to steal watches could be prowling streets again

FEARS have been raised over the return of a female Rolex ripper gang, as mystery distraction thieves allegedly rob and sexually assault two men.

Cops are probing two “linked” incidents of pensioners being robbed by unidentified women while walking in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire.





Both of the robberies happened within days of one another in Aylesbury with both suspects using the same tactics.

The methods employed in the recent robberies have previously been used by a notorious gang of watch thieves.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) has since confirmed it is treating the two Aylesbury incidents as linked.

TVP is also liaising with other forces and “keeping an open mind” as to whether there are links between the Aylesbury robberies and other similar cases.



The crimes have seen the return of the tactics used in a spate of thefts carried out by an all-female gang in the south of England in 2021.

Only one member of the notorious all-female Rolex ripper gang, which played a part in some 15 successful robberies, was ever caught.

The group of crooks used distraction techniques before attempting to touch or “cuddle” their victims while nabbing the valuable timepieces from their wrists.

Stefania Tinica, a Romanian national, was the only member of the group to be caught by cops.



She was taken into custody at Luton Airport as she tried to flee the UK in 2022.

Tinica was jailed for 40 months over her role in a theft in Poole, Dorset and a failed robbery some months earlier in Cheshire.

The theft in Poole saw a £15,930 Rolex Submariner timepiece stolen from a pensioner – the valuable watch was never recovered.

The organised crime gang is believed by cops to be made up of mostly Eastern European women.

They struck in Dorset, Hampshire, West Sussex, Surrey, Gloucestershire and Cheshire.



Most of the cases involved older men targeted by younger women with the same tactics being used in each.

Two new incidents with almost identical circumstances have now been reported to police in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire.

The first victim was attacked on a footpath between Jackson Road and Aston Close just after midday on March 19.



Police say he was approached by a woman who touched him inappropriately over his clothing.

Cops said the attacker then snatched a gold Cubin Link chain from the OAP’s neck, before making off with the jewellery.

The suspect is described as being aged in her early to mid-thirties and around 5ft to 5ft 2ins tall.

She is thought to be Malaysian or Thai in appearance, with an accent – she had her hair tied up at the time of the attack.

Days later, on April 8, another unsuspecting OAP had been walking in Richmond Road when he was approached at around 12:45pm.



The second victim was also touched inappropriately above his clothes and had a Rolex watch stolen from his wrist.

According to the police description, the attacker is a white woman, aged in her twenties or thirties, with long dark hair.

The woman is described as being roughly 5ft tall with a Spanish accent.

In both of the chilling new attacks the victims were offered sexual services before allegedly being sexually assaulted and robbed.

It is not known if there is any link between the recent spate of attacks and those carried out by the all female Rolex ripper gang in 2021.



TVP investigating officer Detective Constable Mandy Cutler said: “This incident has occurred in the middle of the afternoon in Aylesbury.

“(It) has very similar circumstances to a similar incident which occurred last week on 8 April.

“At this stage, I am treating these incidents as linked to each other.

“I am also keeping an open mind as to whether these two incidents are linked to a wider issue of similar such incidents occurring elsewhere in the country.

“We are liaising with partner forces to ascertain whether there are any discernible links to these offences.



“I would urge anybody who has any information or concerns to please get in touch with us.

“You will be listened to and supported, and any information, no matter how significant this may seem, may be crucial in assisting this investigation.”

Separately, TVP told The Sun the force was pursuing the possibility that the thefts were linked to other possible cases.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson said: “It’s very early stages in our investigations, but it is a line of enquiry that our officers are following; although at this stage, there is nothing definitively that can confirm any links.

“The methods used in the two cases in Aylesbury are being treated as linked due to similar modus operandis, and as such, an open mind is being kept on possible wider links, but at this early stage it is not possible to confirm or deny these links.”

News.title: Disturbing truth behind sex offender freed from prison as new ID system unveiled
News.content:
Disturbing truth behind sex offender freed from prison as new ID system unveiled

Deputy PM David Lammy unveiled a new Justice ID system to track every person who enters the prison system from arrest, through the courts, into custody and back into the community

View 2 Images adush Kebatu, the now-deported migrant at the heart of protests in Epping, Essex, was freed in error last year (Image: Essex Police/AFP via Getty Image)

David Lammy has said it is "unacceptable" that 179 prisoners were released from jail in the last year as he vowed to reform the "archaic" prison system.

‌



Mr Lammy, who is deputy PM and Justice Secretary, unveiled a new Justice ID system - a digital identity system - to track every person who enters the prison system from arrest, through the courts, into custody and back into the community.

‌



For the first time, biometric technology - such as fingerprints and facial scans - will be used on all prisoners to verify identities at key points in the system, including releases from custody. Some £82million was pledged to cut release in errors.

‌



The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said the move will replace "shockingly outdated system" where criminals can go by multiple aliases leading to confusion, unnecessary human error and offenders being let out when they should stay behind bars.

Disturbing truth behind three prisoners freed by errors and what happens now READ MORE :

View 2 Images David Lammy has said it is "unacceptable" that 179 prisoners were released from jail in the last year (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Its announcement came as Dame Lynne Owens, a former Metropolitan Police deputy commissioner, said the problem is a “symptom of a broken system” in her independent review of wrongful prisoner releases.

‌



Her review was commissioned afterHadush Kebatu, the now-deported migrant at the heart of protests in Epping, Essex, was freed in error, prompting a police manhunt. Kebatu had been living at the Bell Hotel when he sexually assaulted a 14-year-old girl.

On his wrongful release, Dame Lynne’s report criticised “poor communication between staff” at HMP Chelmsford, and said a disciplinary investigation was carried out into two of its staff – whose identities were not revealed.

She added that the physical prisoner escort paperwork had been marked "not for release" in his case but that this was not on the digital records, which created "inconsistencies on critical paperwork". A gate pass was later incorrectly stated he was for "release".

‌



Dame Lynne added that Kebatu’s victims should have been contacted before social media reports had begun circulating about his mistaken release.

In her foreword, Dame Lynne added: "It would be foolhardy to suggest that all risk in a highly challenging operational environment can be mitigated or negated, but what is less acceptable is a failure to explain the risk choices that are being made at the most senior levels.

"Finally, a plea - this issue spans multiple timeframes and Governments. Now is not the time to throw mud but to consider how Parliament and all those leading the systems can pull together to protect citizens, including those who are retraumatised."

Article continues below

Data released by the MoJ showed 179 inmates were wrongly freed between April 2025 and March 2026. Releases “in error” can include misplaced warrants for imprisonment or remand, sentence miscalculations, or the result of mistakes by courts or other authorities, the MoJ said.

Responding to Dame Lynne's report, Mr Lammy said: “This independent review makes clear the unacceptable rise in release in errors have resulted from a broken system caused by 14 years of underinvestment and overcrowding in our prisons and courts.

“A system broken by over a decade of neglect cannot be fixed overnight, but in addition to the measures we put in place last year, today we are taking action to bring the prison system into the 21st century. “We are rolling out biometrics, a new Justice ID and up to £82million to bear down on these errors and keep the public safe after years of chaos. £20 million of this will be used this year to digitise the archaic paper-based processes we inherited, as well as putting in more checks and more staff in place to stop these mistakes before they happen.”

News.title: Legal advisers caught telling migrants to 'pose as being gay to stay in UK'
News.content:
Legal advisers caught telling migrants to 'pose as being gay to stay in UK'

Migrants are allegedly being given fake cover stories about being gay - as government says anyone caught lying will 'find themselves on a one-way flight out of Britain'

View 3 Images The BBC report showed an interview with 'Tanisa' as part of its investigation

Legal advisers are allegedly charging thousands helping migrants to pose as being gay so they can stay in the UK, a BBC investigation has found.

‌



Migrants whose visas are due to run out are given fake cover stories and instructed in how to obtain fabricated evidence, including supporting letters, photographs and medical reports.

‌



They then apply for asylum claiming to be gay and in fear for their lives if they return to Pakistan or Bangladesh. In response to the BBC investigation, the Home Office said: “Anyone found trying to exploit the system will face the full force of the law, including removal from the UK.”

‌



View 3 Images More than 175 people gathered at an event organised by Worcester LGBT

Meanwhile, Downing Street said migrants found to be lying about their sexuality to claim asylum will "find themselves on a one-way flight out of Britain".

An investigator was told once they won his false case, he could bring his wife over from Pakistan and she could also claim to be a lesbian.

‌



Undercover footage from the BBC shows a meeting for “gay and lesbian asylum seekers” in Beckton, east London. Despite the group’s claims to be a support network, some attending laughed at the idea they were actually gay.

One man, Zeeshan, told the reporter: “Nobody is gay here. I am not gay. Not even 0.01% are gay.” Almost 200 people, travelling from as far as Wales and Birmingham attended the event, organised monthly by Worcester LGBT.

Another firm offering the coaching services demanded £7,000 for a “guaranteed” fake claim. Some advisers boasted they could arrange for people to pretend they’d had gay sexual relationships with the clients.

‌



Organisers behind the scams were caught on camera coaching clients on how to pass their Home Office interviews. The investigation comes as ministers announced the closure of 11 migrant hotels – with 190 remaining. The Government said the shutdowns mark the start of a drive to end the use of hotels for illegal migrants before the next election.

Other migrants involved in the scam were told to visit GPs and feign mental health struggles or even lie about having HIV to bolster their cases.

A lawyer linked to a separate company told how he had helped people claim asylum by pretending to be gay or atheists. His fees increased by up to £3,000 if evidence was wanted.

‌



View 3 Images More than 175 people gathered at an event organised by Worcester LGBT

One adviser, named by the BBC as Tanisa Khan, invited an undercover reporter to her home for an initial consultation. She was filmed in her bedroom saying: “At the moment there is only one route from where you can get a visa and it is open. It is the asylum visa. It is on human rights and it is called gay case or same sex. There is no hope for any other visa.”

She told an undercover reporter she had been helping to bring fake claims for more than 17 years. She charged £2,500, but warned the fee would increase if the claim was refused by the Home Office and went to appeal.

‌



She told him: “There is no check-up to find out if the person is a gay. The main thing is what you say. You just have to tell them that 'I am a gay and it is my reality'. There are a lot of organisations here where there are people like you who are not gay but are applying for the visa. You are not alone."

The reporter had been approached by Tanisa after initially getting in touch with Mazedul Hasan Shakil, a paralegal at Law & Justice Solicitors.

Shakil works at the immigration law firm, based in Birmingham and London, as well as being founder and chairman of Worcester LGBT. After being approached by the BBC, he said the group did not create or support fabricated evidence in asylum claims.

‌



He claimed an investigation into Tanisa’s conduct had been launched. Law & Justice Solicitors said Tanisa was not professionally connected to the firm and that it was investigating “potential unauthorised access”.

Asylum claims topped 100,000 in 2025, with 35% coming from people already in the UK on legal visas that have run out. It is difficult to know exactly how many asylum applications could be fabricated.

A Home Office spokesperson told the BBC: “The asylum system is built on robust safeguards to ensure every claim is rigorously and fairly assessed. Any attempt to misuse protections designed for people fleeing genuine persecution because of their sexuality is deplorable. Abuse is actively uncovered and procedures continually reviewed to shut down misuse.”

‌



Asked about the report, the Prime Minister's official spokesman said: "Any attempt to misuse protections designed for people fleeing genuine persecution because of their sexuality is deplorable.

"Those trying to defraud the British people to enter or remain in the UK will have their asylum claim cancelled, support cut off and find themselves on a one-way flight out of Britain.

"Where unethical and illegal practices are identified and evidence exists, the team will refer legal practitioners to the relevant regulatory body or to the police.

Article continues below

"The asylum system is built on robust safeguards so every claim is rigorous and fairly assessed, abuse is actively uncovered and these procedures are continually reviewed to shut down misuse."

Jonathan Peddie, Executive Director - Investigations, Enforcement and Litigation at the Solicitors Regulation Authority said: "All regulated law firms and solicitors should uphold the high professional standards that we and the public expect of them. This is especially important in areas such as asylum and immigration, where the people involved may be vulnerable.

"We are urgently following up with the SRA-regulated firms identified in the BBC story. If we find evidence that anyone we regulate has acted in ways that contravene their duty to act legally and uphold the law, we will take action."

News.title: 'Amanda Knox has some brass neck to promote her work near Meredith Kercher's home'
News.content:
'Amanda Knox has some brass neck to promote her work near Meredith Kercher's home'

Amanda Knox’s UK visit to promote her work Mouth of the Wolf has reignited anger that she continues to profit from Meredith Kercher’s murder while her family is denied peace

View 4 Images Amanda Knox in her new music video, part of her expanding media career following her acquittal

Amanda Knox is coming to Britain. Not to apologise. Not to pay her respects to a family that has spent nearly two decades living in the shadow of unimaginable grief. She is coming to promote her latest work. To invite strangers to "come say hello."

‌



To offer Britons "two special nights" with Amanda and her husband, just miles from the south London home where Meredith Kercher's parents once tucked their daughter in at night, before Italy took her from them forever.

‌



The sheer brass neck of Knox is almost impressive. She arrives in London to screen her documentary ‘Mouth of the Wolf’, a film directed by her husband Christopher Robinson that revisits the scene of Meredith's murder.

‌



View 4 Images Knox performs stand-up comedy in the US, where she has incorporated her own case into routines for live audiences (Image: Getty Images for ABA)

Amanda Knox to travel to UK to promote film about Meredith Kercher's murder READ MORE :

On making her announcement, Knox revels in selling out the available tickets. "I’ve never been to the UK, but I’m finally going,” she gushes. “It’s fantastic to know that the two screenings I’ll be presenting are already sold out. I’ll soon be releasing some reserved seats to put a few more tickets on sale. Join the waiting list. And thank you, London.”

This from a woman who has turned one of the most horrifying murders in modern British memory into a cottage industry.

‌



Since her final acquittal in 2015, Knox has produced a bestselling memoir, launched a true crime podcast called Hard Knox, executive-produced a Hulu drama series about her own case, alongside Monica Lewinsky, no less and tours as a stand-up comedian. Many have claimed she is mining Meredith's murder for laughs in front of paying crowds in California.

It is okay for the tone-deaf Knox, as she has spoken warmly about finding "the ability to laugh at the bad things that have happened to you and find the absurdity in the human condition." But one thing Knox knows only too well is that to keep up with the times, she constantly needs to reinvent herself. Hence why she has now turned her hand to music and performance, effectively recasting herself as a kind of pop culture figure. It is a catalogue of reinvention built on a single, grim foundation. And that foundation has a name: Meredith Kercher.

The much-loved student was sexually assaulted and stabbed in the throat. Her body was found on the floor of her bedroom, covered by a blood-soaked duvet. She was 21 years old. One wonders what absurdity the Kercher family and her friends find in that.

‌



View 4 Images Meredith Kercher was a 21-year-old Leeds University student when she was murdered in 2007 (Image: PA)

Knox's supporters will say - as they always do - that she is a wronged woman. That she served four years in an Italian prison for a crime she did not commit. That the system failed her. All of that may well be true.

The Italian courts certainly made a spectacular mess of the whole affair, convicting her twice and acquitting her twice in a legal circus that dragged on for the better part of a decade. The Supreme Court of Cassation ultimately pointed to investigative failures and sent everyone home.

‌



But here is what Knox's supporters never quite answer: at what point does a wronged woman's right to rebuild her life become an obligation to consider another family's feelings? At what point does enough become enough?

View 4 Images Knox and Raffaele Sollecito share a kiss outside the Perugia flat as police investigated Kercher’s murder

The Kercher family have never truly been allowed to mourn privately. Every book Knox publishes, every podcast episode she records, every comedy gig she performs and every documentary she screens rips the wound open again.

Article continues below

Meredith's name is never far from Knox's brand, and yet Meredith herself, the laughing, chocolate-loving student from Coulsdon who called her mother every single day, has become little more than a footnote in someone else's redemption story.

And now Knox comes here. To our country. To Meredith’s city. Inviting us to join her for a nice evening out. She does not mention Meredith in her promotional material. She never does. That, perhaps more than anything else, tells you everything you need to know.

News.title: Vatican slams Trump and Vance over 'just war' theory – 'This was before drones'
News.content:
Vatican slams Trump and Vance over 'just war' theory – 'This was before drones'

The Vatican has hit back at Donald Trump and JD Vance, arguing the centuries-old 'just war' theory does not apply to modern conflicts shaped by advanced weaponry

View 4 Images The Vatican has slammed Trump and JD Vance (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The Vatican has issued a sharp rebuke to Donald Trump and JD Vance over their stance on "just war" theory, warning the doctrine was formed "before drones" and is increasingly difficult to justify in modern warfare.

‌



The Vatican's editorial director, Andrea Tornielli, said "just war" was developed centuries ago, when wars were fought with swords - not machine-guided drones.

‌



"This teaching has gradually been enriched and deepened, to the point of recognizing how increasingly difficult it is to claim that a 'just war' exists," Tornielli said.

‌



His comments come after JD Vance pushed back on Pope Leo's claim that God is never on the side of those who wage a war, saying there is a "more than 1,000 year tradition of just war theory".

View 4 Images Vance made the comments during a Turning Point USA event yesterday

Speaking at a Turning Point USA event at the University of Georgia yesterday, Vance added: "We can, of course, have disagreements about whether this or that conflict is just."

‌



The remarks were prompted after Donald Trump branded Pope Leo "weak on crime" and "terrible for foreign policy" in response to the pontiff's criticism of the US-Israeli led war on Iran.

Modern warfare poses a "reality that raises moral questions of dramatic intensity," Tornielli said in his response to the vice president. "There has been a growing awareness that war is not a path to be followed," he wrote.

US Cardinal Robert McElroy, the archbishop of Washington, has said the US-Israeli war in Iran failed to meet the minimum criteria for the war to be considered morally just.

‌



View 4 Images President Donald Trump called Pope Leo XIV 'weak on crime' and 'terrible for foreign policy' on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

Such criteria would have included that it was a response to an imminent threat, that the US and Israel had clearly articulated their intentions or that the benefits would outweigh the harm.

Speaking to crowds on Tuesday, Vance questioned: "How do you say that God is never on the side of those who wield the sword?", citing the example of US troops liberating France from the Nazis and freeing prisoners from concentration camps.

‌



"I think it's very, very important for the pope to be careful when he talks about matters of theology," Vance said. "If you're going to opine on matters of theology, you've got to be careful. You've got to make sure it's anchored in the truth and that's one of the things that I try to do and it's certainly something I would expect from the clergy."

Meanwhile earlier today, Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image depicting himself beside a Jesus-like figure.

View 4 Images The X post that Donald Trump shared on his Truth Social account on Wednesday (Image: @Dkelly4congress/X)

Article continues below

The US president posted a screenshot on his Truth Social account of an X post showing a Jesus-like figure embracing him - in another provocative move amid his rift with Pope Leo XIV, a vocal critic of the US and Israeli war on Iran.

The post, from an account named "Irish for Trump" (@Dkelly4congress), depicts a long-haired, bearded figure resembling Jesus standing closely beside Trump with both arms around him.

The X post reads: "I was never a very religious man... but doesn’t it seem, with all these satanic, demonic, child sacrificing monsters being exposed... that God might be playing his Trump card!"

News.title: Amanda Knox to travel to UK to promote film about Meredith Kercher's murder
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Amanda Knox to travel to UK to promote film about Meredith Kercher's murder

Amanda Knox, twice convicted and twice acquitted of the murder of British student Meredith Kercher, is to travel to Britain for the first time to screen her documentary

View 5 Images Knox has built a high-profile media career from her past, with books, podcasts and appearances drawing on the notoriety of the Kercher case (Image: Matt Licari/Invision/AP)

Amanda Knox is to travel to the UK for the first time — inviting Brits to "come say hello" and join her for “two special nights” just miles from where Meredith Kercher lived.

‌



The American, twice convicted and twice acquitted of the murder of the Leeds University student, is due to arrive next week to promote her film ‘Mouth of the Wolf’. It comes after her podcast about Lucy Letby, in which she said she felt a "recognition" with the case, sparked anger.

‌



Announcing her visit, Knox gushed: "I’ve never been to the UK, but I’m finally going. It’s fantastic to know that the two screenings I’ll be presenting are already sold out! I’ll soon be releasing some reserved seats to put a few more tickets on sale! Join the waiting list! And thank you, London!"

‌



The documentary, directed by her husband Christopher Robinson, captures her return to the scene where Meredith was murdered. It also features some original songs for the soundtrack sung by Knox, for which she has produced videos.

The now mother-of-two, who has transformed her wrongful conviction into a lucrative career spanning books, podcasts, film and stand-up comedy, has promised Brits the offer to meet her just miles from where Meredith lived with her parents. The 38-year-old will be in London on April 21 and 22. She personally invited Brits to attend, posting: "We're excited to share that Mouth of the Wolf will be screening in London for two special nights on April 21 and 22.

View 5 Images Meredith Kercher was a 21-year-old Leeds University student when she was murdered in 2007 (Image: ITALIAN POLICE/AFP via Getty Ima)

‌



Meredith Kercher’s family lawyer slams Amanda Knox over new Disney murder drama READ MORE :

“These intimate screenings are a chance to experience the film in a city that has long embraced bold, thought-provoking storytelling. If you're in London, or know someone who is, we'd love to see you there. Amanda and Chris will be taking questions after the film. Join the waitlist as more tickets will be released soon.”

‌



The free screenings are to be held at the Greenwich Picturehouse. To her supporters, Knox is a wronged woman who spent four years in an Italian prison for a crime she did not commit. But to her critics, she is seen as someone who has monetised Meredith’s brutal killing.

Since her final acquittal by Italy's Supreme Court of Cassation in 2015, Knox has rarely been out of the public eye. She has written a memoir, hosted a true crime podcast called Hard Knox, served as executive producer on a Hulu drama series about her own case and, most recently, taken to the stand-up comedy circuit - joking about her murder conviction to paying audiences in California.

Meredith’s family, who lived in south London, have long spoken of their discomfort at the way the 21-year-old’s name has been attached to Knox's personal brand. While the American continues to make money from her experience, the Kerchers have faced every interview, anniversary and new Knox project as a fresh reminder of her death in November 2007.

‌



Meredith was a popular student studying at the University of Leeds when she took up an exchange place in Perugia, Italy. She moved into a flat in September 2007, sharing with two Italian women and Knox, then a 20-year-old from Seattle attending the University for Foreigners.

The two young women got along, visited a EuroChocolate festival together and frequently socialised. On the night of November 1, 2007, Meredith was murdered in her bedroom. Her body was found on the floor, covered by a blood-soaked duvet. She had been sexually assaulted and stabbed in the neck.

View 5 Images Knox and Raffaele Sollecito share a kiss outside the Perugia flat as police investigated the murder of Meredith Kercher - images that sparked widespread outrage

‌



While Italian police worked the murder scene, Knox was photographed kissing her boyfriend of one week, Raffaele Sollecito, outside the flat. The images of the couple embracing caused widespread revulsion. Knox later said she had been in shock.

The couple were taken in for questioning within days of the murder. Knox later said she was interrogated without a lawyer or a qualified interpreter, bullied and physically struck by police. During that interrogation, she made a statement implicating Patrick Lumumba, the Congolese owner of the bar where she worked part-time, in the murder.

Lumumba was arrested and held for two weeks before being released. That false accusation would haunt her legally for years to come.

‌



In 2009, Knox was convicted of Meredith's murder and sentenced to 26 years in prison. Sollecito received 25 years. A third defendant, Rudy Guede, whose DNA and bloody footprints were found throughout the crime scene, was tried separately on a fast-track procedure and convicted of sexual assault and murder.

His sentence was eventually reduced to 16 years, and he was released on early release in December 2020. Knox publicly opposed that release.

In 2011, Knox's conviction was overturned on appeal, and she was freed, returning immediately to the United States. Then, in 2013, Italy's Supreme Court declared the acquittal null and void, citing "manifest illogicalities," and ordered a retrial.

‌



View 5 Images Promotional image for Mouth of the Wolf, the film by Knox and her husband, revisiting the scene of the crime at the centre of the case

In 2014, a Florence appeals court convicted her of murder for a second time.

Knox remained in America throughout, refusing to return to Italy. Then, in March 2015, the Supreme Court of Cassation definitively acquitted her, invoking reasonable doubt and pointing to what it called "sensational investigative failures" and "culpable omissions" by Italian authorities. It was ordered that no further trial be held.

‌



In June 2024, Knox returned to Italy for only the second time since her release - to face yet another slander trial in Florence over her false accusation against Lumumba.

An Italian appellate court upheld the conviction. She was not sent back to prison, having already served the equivalent sentence during her original detention, but the conviction stood as a lasting stain.

Knox told the court: "I am very sorry that I was not strong enough to resist the pressure of police. I didn't know who the murderer was. I had no way to know."

Article continues below

Ever since her first release, Knox has built a career out of Meredith’s murder. Her memoir was a bestseller. Her podcast attracted a loyal audience. When Hulu produced a dramatised series about her case, "The Twisted Tale of Amanda Knox”, she was not merely a subject but an executive producer, alongside Monica Lewinsky. She said she had "chills" watching actress Grace Van Patten portray her on screen.

View 5 Images Knox in a music video appearance, part of a growing list of media projects that have followed her public life

Then came the stand-up comedy. Knox began performing last summer, working Meredith's murder into her material. She opened for comedian Nikki Glaser in Seattle in front of a crowd of 3,000 people after Glaser spotted footage of one of her early gigs on Instagram. Knox told that crowd: "Here's how I look at it." She has spoken of finding "the ability to laugh at the bad things that have happened to you and find the absurdity in the human condition."

News.title: Fears grow that UK families could be impacted by summer holiday cancellations
News.content:
Fears grow that UK families could be impacted by summer holiday cancellations

The risk of flight cancellations on some routes is looming because of the ongoing Strait of Hormuz blockade which has led to soaring jet fuel prices

View 3 Images Travellers risk being left high and dry if airlines begin cancelling flights due to Iran war (Image: Getty)

UK airlines could soon start cancelling flights because of potential jet fuel shortages - potentially hitting millions of families in the peak summer getaway.

‌



Concerns are growing that holidaymakers and other travellers could begin to be impacted if airlines pull flights to preserve fuel supplies in the wake of disruption caused by the Middle East conflict.

‌



It raises the risk that British families aiming to take half term breaks and the summer holidays could face major disruption, although industry chiefs insisted there were no signs of shortages at this stage.

‌



Economist Thomas Pugh noted that some smaller airlines had already cancelled routes and added fuel surcharges. “It won’t be long before larger ones follow suit, as they have in Asia,” said Mr Pugh, of audit, tax and consulting firm RSM UK”, adding: “that’s demand destruction in action.”

easyJet Portugal update as airline issues warning over new 'allowance' rule READ MORE :

View 3 Images A hit to jet fuel supplies risks leading to flight cancellations (Image: ANIK)

Ryanair boss Michael O’Leary said at the start of April that it may be forced to cancel 10% of its flights this summer. He told ITV News: “We’re all facing an unknown scenario. And we are certainly looking at maybe having to cancel 5% to 10% of flights through May, June and July.”

‌



Rico Luman, a senior economist at the investment bank ING, said: “Smaller airports will be in a weaker position than the main hubs because of less storage facilities on site. It’s limited for now, but if nothing changes and the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked for several more weeks to come there could be some bottlenecks over the course of May.

View 3 Images Ryanair boss Michael O'Leary has warned between 5% of and 10% of flights from May could be cancelled (Image: Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

“The UK is also relatively sensitive to shortages as it produces just a minority of its own consumption, so dependency on imports is relatively high,” he added.

‌



The threat comes after airport bosses recently warned that jet fuel stocks could run short within three weeks if oil supplies do not start to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.

Airports Council International Europe said in a letter to the EU’s energy and transport commissioners: “If the passage through the strait of Hormuz does not resume in any significant and stable way within the next three weeks, systemic jet fuel shortage is set to become a reality for the EU.”

Some airlines have already begun adding surcharges to help offset a jump in fuel costs. Virgin Atlantic has slapped on a £50 levy to economy fares, £180 on premium and £360 on first class.

‌



The risk of possible flight groundings comes amid a mounting fuel supply crunch triggered by the Iran war.

Europe’s oil and gas industry has shrunk dramatically over the past 25 years, with North Sea production having dwindled and more than 30 refineries - 16% of refining capacity - shuttered across the continent. The contraction reflects a combination of shrinking domestic demand, rising overseas competition and, increasingly over the past decade, a government-led drive to curb greenhouse gas emissions. The upshot is that Europe has become heavily reliant on energy imports.

Europe is more dependent on jet fuel imports than for any other transport fuel. The region consumed about 1.6 million barrels per day last year, of which roughly 500,000 were imported, according to the International Energy Agency. Around 75% of those imports came from the Middle East.

‌



Refineries in Asia, which source about 60% of their crude imports from the Middle East, were forced to scale back operations by some three million barrels per day between February and April, according to the IEA.

With Asian demand competing for scarce barrels, benchmark European jet fuel prices surged to an all-time high in mid-March.

Europe has struggled to replace the lost Middle Eastern barrels, with jet fuel imports down 13% from the 2025 average, according to analytics firm Kpler.

‌



The last cargoes of jet fuel from the Middle East are now approaching Europe, meaning that finding replacement barrels will soon prove even more challenging – and more expensive.

With supplies critically tight, airlines and oil importers face two options: bid up prices to compete with Asia for scarce barrels, or cut consumption.

Lufthansa boss Carsten Spohr warned this week that grounding aircraft “may be unavoidable” as shortages hit major airports.

Article continues below

Trade body Airlines UK, in a statement issued at the weekened, insisted there was no cause for concern at this stage. It said: “UK airlines are currently not seeing disruption to jet fuel supply, in part due to the UK’s diverse fuel supply, and continue to engage with fuel suppliers and Government to monitor the situation.”

An airline source said it was difficult to say at this stage whether fares will have to rise, but added “higher fuel costs will be hard for airlines to completely absorb.”

It came amid threats of fuel protests on motorways across the UK because of the soaring cost of petrol and diesel since the Iran war erupted. Social media posts claimed farmers were planning to block major motorway junctions. It is claimed disruption could extend to London in the coming weeks.

News.title: Honeymoon shark attack in Maldives as man fighting for life and 'flesh torn off'
News.content:
Honeymoon shark attack in Maldives as man fighting for life and 'flesh torn off'

The holidaymaker was attacked by a shark while on his honeymoon in the Maldives, suffering extreme blood loss and having his leg amputated after being airlifted to hospital

View 2 Images The man was attacked while on honeymoon in the Maldives (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

A tourist is fighting for his life after being attacked by a shark while on his honeymoon in the Maldives.

‌



The holidaymaker suffered extreme blood loss and had to have his leg amputated after being airlifted to hospital. The victim of the attack has been identified as a Spanish gynaecologist called Borja.

‌



Local newspaper El Periodico Mediterraneo said he came from Alicante and had just married a woman from the area called Ana before they headed to the Indian Ocean paradise for their first holiday together as man and wife. Quoting a source close to Ana's family today, the paper said the shark "took all the flesh from the knee down off her husband's leg" with just "one bite".

‌



The horror attack is believed to have unfolded off Kooddoo, one of the inhabited islands of Gaafu Alif Atoll, on Monday afternoon.

View 2 Images The man had to have his leg amputated after the attack (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The victim is thought to have been part of a group that entered the water near the Kooddoo fish processing plant - a location known for high shark activity.

He was initially taken to the Ga. Atoll Hospital before being airlifted to Male, the densely-populated capital of the Maldives, and admitted to an intensive care unit at ADK Hospital.

Local reports claim the Kooddoo facility had not dumped fish waste for around a week, with one source quoted as saying: "The sharks were likely in a heightened state of hunger and anticipation. When the group jumped in, the entry itself may have triggered a predatory response."

Article continues below

A family member had already lodged a formal complaint against the firm that organised their group excursion, accusing it of negligence, according to local reports.

Relatives of Ana, described as the daughter of a well-known Castellon businessman, have since flown out to the Maldives to comfort her. The family acquaintance told the Spanish daily: "They are trying to save Borja, he’s in intensive care, but the medical conditions there are very precarious."

Kooddoo is home to a four-star hotel called the Mercure Maldives Kooddoo Resort, which is a popular honeymoon destination.

News.title: Donald Trump increasingly ‘cut off from reality’ as US faces ‘civil emergency’
News.content:
Donald Trump increasingly ‘cut off from reality’ as US faces ‘civil emergency’

Michael Wolff, who has written four books about Donald Trump, says the US president seems increasingly 'cut off' from reality as his Truth Social posts become more and more deranged

View 2 Images Donald Trump's Truth Social posts have become increasingly deranged (Image: Celal Gunes/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Donald Trump is becoming increasingly “cut off from reality” and it could constitute a “civil emergency”, according to a biographer who has observed the US president up close.

‌



Trump has always been prone to bizarre outbursts on his social platform Truth Social, but they have undoubtedly intensified since the onset of the war with Iran. Prime examples have been him declaring a “whole civilisation will die” and demanding Iran “open the f**king Strait [of Hormuz]”.

‌



And his posts haven’t become any more calm since the ceasefire was agreed. In recent days he has shared an AI image of himself depicted as Jesus and taken aim at Pope Leo - before refusing to apologise.

‌



View 2 Images Trump shared this bizarre image, seemingly depicting himself as Jesus (Image: @realDonaldTrump/Truth Social)

Author Michael Wolff, who has written four books about the US president, told The Daily Beast's ‘Inside Trump's Head’ podcast that these outbursts show Trump is becoming “more and more distinct from, cut-off from, separate from reality”.

He said: “We have seen 10 years of erratic behavior, but I think it is coming faster and more furious in these past number of weeks, probably prompted by the war, which is going terribly, of course, and he doesn’t know what to do, and he doesn’t know how to get out of it.”

‌



Wolff - who was granted access to the White House during Trump’s first term - believes his recent meltdowns have been caused by a host of factors, not just the Iran war, including “Minneapolis, ICE, the failing economy, the dimwits that surround him, which he has now been forced to fire”.

He went on: "So I think he is in a corner, and that has meant he’s flailing out erratically… There is every reason to believe, and for every reasonable person to believe, that something is seriously off here and dangerous.”

As such, he suggested the Trump administration - and the US as a whole - might be at a crisis point, adding: “If you stop seeing it as a reasonable enterprise - that is a civil emergency.”

Article continues below

It comes as Trump today shared another AI-generated image depicting himself in Jesus-like imagery, paired with a bizarre caption from the original poster stating that "God might be playing his Trump card".

The US president posted a screenshot of an X post showing a Jesus-like figure embracing him. The post, from an account named "Irish for Trump" (@Dkelly4congress), depicts a long-haired, bearded figure resembling Jesus standing closely beside Trump with both arms around him.

News.title: British doubles legend Jamie Murray retires from tennis
News.content:
Murray will be remembered for his razor-sharp volleying skills and the preposterous angles he conjured at the net. His returns were often unorthodox and he was fond of a lobbed service return to unsettle opponents.

Alongside his triumphs, Murray has been a staunch defender of doubles players and frequently demanded they be shown more respect.

"Doubles has its place in the game - it's not the golden ticket that singles is, but it's undervalued by the tour," Murray told BBC Sport.

"As these events go longer and longer they need content, and doubles supports that."

Murray said he was proud to have represented his hometown of Dunblane and the country of Scotland at the highest level.

"There is no history of tennis and no environment of tennis [in Scotland]," Murray told BBC Sport.

"I'd imagine the odds were against us from the start but we were able to make some good things happen."

His mother Judy thought Jamie had the better hand-eye co-ordination of her sons when young. Jamie and Andy briefly became rivals as tennis players - and also while wrestling.

Judy once recalled: "Andy's favourite [wrestler] was The Rock and Jamie's was Stone Cold Steve Austin, and they used to create these bouts that they saw on the television. They used to wrestle each other on the duvet and thump each other with pillows, and create these belts and make up their own rules and scoring systems."

Jamie is 15 months older than Andy, and as his early dominance on the tennis court started to fade Andy says he quite literally bore the brunt.

"We were coming back from Solihull in the minibus and I'd beaten Jamie in the final, I think, of the under-12s, so basically I was winding him up about that and my hand was on the hand rest," he said in 2015.

"We were sitting next to each other and he just basically punched me on the hand - I lost my fingernail and I've still got the scars to show for it."

Despite some defeats against Andy, Jamie was still very much on track for a professional singles career until a negative experience at an LTA training school in Cambridge in his very early teens.

He struggled with living away from home and the elite training environment, and even though he has never sought to blame the LTA, his forehand suffered and he has said he was never quite the same player again.

A California nurse has won a $300,000 lawsuit against cruise giant Carnival Corp., after claiming the ship’s bar staff served her so much tequila she fell over and severely injured herself.

Diana Sanders, 45, was given “at least 14 shots of tequila” in just over eight-and-a-half hours during the cruise from Los Angeles to Hawaii and Mexico in January 2024, according to a lawsuit obtained by The Miami Herald.

“Due to her inebriated state that was caused by this over-service of alcohol ... [Sanders] suffered a severe fall,” according to the complaint.

The fall resulted in “severe injuries, including, but not limited to, a concussion, headaches, a possible traumatic brain injury, back injuries, tailbone injuries, bruising, and other injuries.”

Lawyers for Sanders argued that once she had become visibly intoxicated, she should have been cut off by bartenders.

In their verdict the jury found that 60 percent of the responsibility for the incident lay with Carnival, and 40 percent lay with Sanders.

A California woman has won a $300,000 lawsuit against cruise giant Carnival Corp., after claiming the ship’s bar staff served her so much tequila she fell over and severely injured herself ( Getty/iStock )

Crew members had a reasonable duty of care towards Sanders, including “the responsibility ... to supervise and/or assist passengers aboard the vessel who Carnival knew, or should have known, were engaging, or were likely to engage in behavior potentially dangerous to themselves or others abroad the vessel,” according to the documents seen by The Herald.

She was awarded $300,000 in damages, exceeding the $250,000 requested.

The Independent has contacted Carnival Corp. for comment on the case and verdict.

“Carnival Corporation respectfully disagrees with the verdict and believes there are grounds for a new trial and appeal, which it will pursue,” a spokesperson for the cruise company told The Herald.

The company had previously sought to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that Sanders “fails to identify any crew member who over-served her or which bar she consumed alcohol at for Carnival to have the ability to identify its bartenders” according to court documents.

“Therefore, the over-service of alcohol count should be dismissed for failure to sufficiently identify a negligent employee.”

Carnival’s lawyers added that Sanders “does not sufficiently allege that any crew member knew or should have known that Plaintiff was intoxicated. ... There are no allegations regarding Plaintiff stumbling, sleeping at a bar, slurring her words, or exhibiting any other intoxicated-like behaviors.”

Successful cases of complaints against cruise companies are rare, with many failing even to reach the courtroom.

Incoming Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar coolly ramped up pressure on the country’s president to resign on Wednesday, moments after being asked to form a government.

Magyar, 45, shared a picture of himself alongside president Dr Tamas Sulyok, standing in front of the flags of Hungary and the European Union with their hands crossed at the Sándor Palace.

He tagged the president, an ally of his predecessor Viktor Orbán, in the post, saying he was “unworthy of representing the unity of the Hungarian nation”, “unfit to serve as the guardian of legality” and “not fit to serve as a moral authority or a role model”.

“Following the formation of the new government, Tamás Sulyok must leave office immediately,” Magyar wrote. He told reporters that Sulyok said he would “consider” the request during their meeting, which he described as otherwise amicable.

Magyar threatened that if Sulyok does not resign, he would use his party's big mandate to amend the constitution and other legislation and to force him from office, along with other "puppets" who had been appointed by the Orbán government.

Magyar separately shared a video from the palace of himself and his team watching Orbán, alone, pacing on an adjacent balcony. Magyar framed the image with his hands and said “absolute cinema”, with Linkin Park’s ‘What I’ve Done’ overlaid.

open image in gallery Peter Magyar shared a photograph of himself with president Dr. Tamás Sulyok ( Peter Magyar / X )

Magyar’s TISZA (Respect and Freedom) party won a landslide victory in Sunday’s election, ending Orbán’s 16-year reign and promising to clamp down on corruption and ease rule of law concerns in a bid to repair ties to the EU and unfreeze billions of euros in withheld funding.

"I told the president [Sulyok] .... that Hungarian people have voted for a change of regime," Magyar said. He said Sulyok told him during a meeting Magyar described as otherwise amicable that he would "consider" the request.

The election winner said that his cabinet could be sworn in by mid-May as he unveiled plans to rapidly repeal years of autocratic drift in order to avoid the loss of some 10 billion euros of EU pandemic recovery funding before the deadline in August.

Anti-corruption measures included joining the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, restoring and strengthening the independence of the judiciary and investigative authorities, and restoring media and academic freedoms.

open image in gallery Outgoing Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban arrives at the Presidential Sandor Palace in Budapest on April 15 ( AFP/Getty )

As part of wider moves to restore press freedoms after taking office next month, Magyar said he would suspend state media news broadcasts, which critics at home and abroad say became a government mouthpiece under Orbán.

“Every Hungarian deserves a public service media that broadcasts the truth,” Magyar said on Kossuth state radio, where Orbán had been a weekly guest while opposition politicians rarely got invited.

“We will need a little time to pass a new media law, a new media authority and setting up the professional conditions for state media to actually do what it is meant to do.”

Side effects from weight loss drugs, including ”Ozempic face”, are behind a surge in facial cosmetic surgery procedures in the UK, surgeons have said.

New data from the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS) shows procedures including facelifts and eyelid surgery are on the rise, while breast augmentations and abdominoplasties, known as tummy tucks, are falling.

Surgeons said one reason behind the surge is a rising awareness of the side effects of weight-loss medication, including the gaunt or aged appearance that can be caused by rapid weight loss through GLP-1 drugs, often called “Ozempic face”.

open image in gallery Facial procedures are on the rise, new data from the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS) shows ( Getty/iStock )

Former BAAPS president Rajiv Grover, who compiled the audit, said a “new era of openness” on social media has also helped change perceptions of facial surgery.

Despite a sharp decline in demand, the data shows breast augmentation remains the most popular form of cosmetic surgery in the UK, with 4,761 procedures in 2025. But it is now closely followed by breast reduction surgery, with 4,673 procedures last year.

Surgeries for superficial gluteal lipofilling (SGL), a safer alternative to traditional Brazilian butt lifts (BBL), also plummeted by 38 per cent over the last year.

Surgeons said the data shows demand for an exaggerated hourglass silhouette may be falling in what they called a “growing shift towards comfort and natural proportions”.

open image in gallery Doctors have warned accelerated ageing is a side effect of weight loss injections ( Reuters )

Meanwhile, face and neck lifts rose by 11 per cent, brow lifts by 27 per cent, and eyelid surgery was up eight per cent.

But the 26,840 cosmetic procedures performed in 2025 is an overall two per cent drop from the previous year.

Dr Grover said: “Social media has allowed people to see what modern facial surgery really looks like with subtle, natural and restorative results, driven by the newer techniques of deep plane facelift and deep plane neck lift surgery.

He added patients are “increasingly” seeking longer-term solutions which they have often seen promoted by celebrities on social media.

“Awareness of the side effects of weight-loss drugs such as “Ozempic face” have also driven medical reasons for patients seeking facial aesthetic procedures,” he continued.

Doctors have previously warned over unwanted side effects such as facial ageing from GLP-1 drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy. Speaking to The Independent, Dr Sebastian Bejma, advanced aesthetic doctor at the Dr Bejma Medical Clinic in Leeds, explained the sheer speed of weight loss using GLP-1s can make it hard for skin to shrink back the way it usually does with diet and exercise-focused weight loss.

Rapid weight loss can also negatively impact levels of collagen which Dr Bejma says “provides rigidity and strength to the skin”, and elastin which “allows it to be flexible and retract back to shape”.

Mr Naveen Cavale, consultant plastic surgeon at Real Clinic said the skin acts like a deflating balloon during rapid weight loss, causing accelerated ageing. “If you let the air out gradually, it probably has time to shrink back down almost to the size that it was when it first came out of the packet.

“And if people lose weight gradually, your skin [and] its elasticity has time to recover. Your skin can regenerate.” But if not, you can end up with “excess hanging skin”.

Barcelona forward Raphinha has issued an apology for a controversial gesture directed at Atletico Madrid fans following his team’s elimination from the Champions League quarter-finals.

The Brazil international, who was sidelined with a hamstring injury for Tuesday’s decisive match, was seen making a "robbed" sign with his hands and later told reporters that Barcelona had been "robbed" over the two legs.

He also gestured towards Atletico supporters, seemingly indicating they would be eliminated in the next round, appearing to tell fans "you are out."

Raphinha later expressed regret for his actions towards the crowd.

"I apologise for my gesture, which does not reflect my values or character," he told DAZN on Wednesday. "It was an act in a moment of tension, in response to a fan who was disrespecting me."

He is now likely to face disciplinary action from Uefa for his conduct at the Metropolitano stadium.

open image in gallery Atletico goalkeeper Juan Musso hit back at Raphinha's claim that Barcelona were 'robbed' ( Getty )

Despite the apology for his gesture, Raphinha stood firm on his criticism of the match officials.

"To me, it was ‘robbed’," he reiterated to reporters on Tuesday. "Not only this match, but the other one as well. The refereeing was very bad. Incredible the decisions that they made. Atletico made a lot of fouls and the referee didn’t show a single yellow card."

Atletico goalkeeper Juan Musso dismissed Raphinha’s accusations as "nonsense”.

"I respect everyone's opinion, but let's not say that it was a robbery, because it wasn't like that," Musso countered. "We won it on the field. We won 2-0 on the road.

“It’s a team that we respect a lot and are very motivated to play against. It’s a great team, but I think that to talk about robbery is just crazy."

Barcelona president Joan Laporta echoed Raphinha’s sentiments, describing the refereeing as "shameful" and "inadmissible." The club has indicated plans to lodge a formal complaint with Uefa.

Barcelona secured a 2-1 victory on Tuesday but were ultimately eliminated 3-2 on aggregate, having lost the first leg 2-0 at home.
